title: proofbundle eval-claim v0.1
description: The canonical payload of an eval receipt: proves suite S scored comparator threshold T (passed), carrying only salted commitments to model/dataset identifiers.

threshold.description: decimal STRING, never a JSON float

assurance_level.description: how much a PASS is worth: self-attested by the issuer, third-party checked, independently reproduced, or produced in an attested enclave. Signed into the claim.

evaluation_card_sha256.description: optional sha256 (hex) digest of an external, human-readable Eval Card document describing the evaluation's methodology (see EVAL_CLAIM.md, docs/proofbundle.evalcard) — additive, backward-compatible; mechanically identical to prereg_sha256 (a verifier re-hashes the disclosed document and checks it matches). Aligns with the Hugging Face EvalEval Coalition's Evaluation Cards concept (arXiv:2606.09809) rather than inventing a proofbundle-specific card format.

provenance.description: optional run provenance (harness, git_hash, task_version, n_shot, stderr, run_attempts, aborted_runs, methodology_sha256, benchjack_audit_report_sha256) — additive, backward-compatible; 5.0.0 adds, for every harness-REPORTED version field (harness_version, task_version, promptfoo_version), an explicit `<field>_status` with the three literals reported/not_reported/not_bound and a `<field>_status_reason` that is mandatory whenever the status is not `reported` — so the ABSENCE of a version field stops carrying two meanings at once. The version field itself is unchanged and stays absent when nothing was reported

samples.description: Optional per-sample Merkle commitment (v1.5): RFC 6962 SHA-256 root over one leaf per sample; leaves are RFC 9901-style salted disclosures. n MUST equal the claim's n.

root_b64.description: Standard base64 of the 32-byte samples tree root.

coverage.description: Optional coverage block (5.1, additive, backward-compatible): what the evaluation EXAMINED, not merely that the receipt is intact. Without it, a cryptographically clean receipt over an empty check set is indistinguishable from a clean receipt over a full one — integrity does not imply coverage. Optional as a WHOLE, but COMPLETE when present: partial coverage numbers are worse than none, because a missing denominator invites the reader to assume the ratio is 1. Definitions are disjoint: population_size is the set that SHOULD have been examined; evaluated_count is how many of them produced a verdict; unresolved_count is how many did not (attempted or not). The remainder (population_size - evaluated_count - unresolved_count) is the deliberately EXCLUDED set. evaluated_count MUST equal the claim's n, mirroring the samples.n == n rule: n is already the size the aggregate was computed over, so a second, free-floating number would be a second truth about the same quantity. HONEST LIMIT: these are issuer-DECLARED counts. The signature binds them to the issuer and makes them tamper-evident; it does not make them correct.

population_size.description: size of the set that should have been examined

evaluated_count.description: how many of the population produced a verdict; MUST equal the claim's n

unresolved_count.description: how many of the population did not produce a verdict
